checks.name: why_it_matters
checks.note: 4 per matched defect with a correct consequence

finding.evidence: “The March incident was a single certificate event; all 15,500 failed transactions are attributed to the certificate”
finding.why_it_matters: The source pack establishes two distinct incidents with different causes: the 2 March certificate failure and the 4 March failed rollback. This summary misstates the events and attributes the second incident’s impact to the wrong cause.

finding.evidence: “The remediation plan was approved by the Board on 8 March” and “The platform team has taken over certificate management, and the quarterly audit is in place”
finding.why_it_matters: The plan is explicitly marked draft, not approved, with approval pending; the source pack does not establish that its actions have been implemented. The memo falsely presents a proposal and unverified actions as decided and completed.

finding.evidence: “Both incidents had the same root cause” and “The 4 March event was a follow-on certificate failure”
finding.why_it_matters: INC-032 was caused by a failed rollback of CHG-441, unrelated to the certificate incident. Treating it as a follow-on certificate failure gives the Board a false account of the incident and its causes.

finding.evidence: “The certificate alert was re-enabled on 2 March, so the control is restored”
finding.why_it_matters: The source pack says the alert was disabled and does not establish that it was re-enabled. The Board therefore cannot rely on this memo to conclude the control has been restored.

finding.evidence: “No further verification is needed because the plan is approved and the control is restored”
finding.why_it_matters: Neither premise is supported: the plan remains unapproved and restoration of the alert is unverified. Recommending closure without checking these matters could leave unresolved incident actions and controls.

false_defects.evidence: “The audit note confirms the single-event framing”; “The status page shows the certificate cause for both entries, which confirms the shared root cause”
false_defects.why_it_matters: The audit note rejects the single-event framing, and the status page says its cause field was auto-filled from a template. Presenting these as confirmation obscures the evidence that the incidents were separate and had different causes.

false_defects.evidence: “Close both incidents” and “The Board can note the closure at its next meeting”
false_defects.why_it_matters: The memo never establishes whether either incident is already closed, and the source pack provides no closure status. It therefore does not answer the COO’s central question.
